english.title: Possess / have custody of a fighting dog
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your possession or custody a dog to which section 1 of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 applied, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF DOG..).
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(3) and (7) of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
possessed/had custody of fighting dog

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Possession of a fighting dog under a power of seizure or in accordance with an order for destruction is excepted.
(ii) DOGS BORN BEFORE 30TH November 1991 and in respect of which the conditions specified in Articles 4/5 of the Dangerous Dogs Compensation and Exemption Schemes Order 1991 (SI 1991/1744) are complied with are exempt.
(iii) Section 1 of the Act applies to the Pit Bull terrier, the Japanese Tosa and any other type designated by order of the Secretary of State. The Dogo Argentino and Fila Braziliero were designated by SI 1991/1743.
(iv) Where known, any detail as to the identity of the particular dog in question may be included at **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF DOG..) (e.g. registration number) in addition to the breed.
(v) A court may make a destruction order and disqualify the offender from having custody of a dog (section 4 as amended by the Dangerous Dogs (Amendment) Act 1997).
(vi) A court may make a contingent destruction order, see section 4A.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
